findings.reason: the census and measure sections should name the owner they extend (or state why it cannot carry the job), which changes §2/§3's deliverable text and prevents a third parallel reader.
findings.text: §2 commissions a sentence census and §3 a transcript token measure with no recorded search for prior machinery; the token measure re-derives an account `reckon/crew/metering.py` already holds, and the census re-derives the skill-text assertions `tests/test_skill_contracts.py` holds, so the plan could have extended both

findings.reason: §3 must re-run the census against the rewritten skill, and with two tokenisers the before/after counts the ≤4,000- and ≤12,000-word ceilings are judged against are not comparable, so the plan should say which counter is canonical before the rewrite.
findings.text: the §2 capability is spread across seven scripts in four figure directories — `classify-rules-in-the-skill/{scan_binding.py,reconcile_coverage.py,render_dispositions.py}`, `classify-rules-in-the-other-references/{sentence_counts.py,rows.py,render.py}`, `classify-rules-reconcile/reconcile_skill.py` — of which two (`scan_binding.py`, `sentence_counts.py`) independently implement the identical stated sentence-splitting method and two (`reconcile_coverage.py`, `reconcile_skill.py`) independently reconcile candidates to rows, with no shared module and no single entry point

findings.reason: §3's re-census needs a reconciler that still runs at the post-rewrite tree, so §2's coverage check should be one placeable script rather than a scratch-bound one-off.
findings.text: the reconciler hardcodes an absolute worktree path (`/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/.reckon-worktrees/reckon-c8f839407e49/s25-coord/classify-rules-reconcile`) and reads its inputs from a `/tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/...` directory, so it is a one-shot script that cannot run against the rewritten text §3 produces and cannot be re-run by any later reader of the fragment

findings.reason: the plan should extend `reckon/crew/metering.py` (or name why its transcript grammar cannot carry a skill-load window) so §3's grade is reconcilable with the metering the rest of reckon reports.
findings.text: the token measure the §3 done-when is graded by reads Claude Code transcripts under `~/.claude/projects` and sums `input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens` per request, which is exactly the Claude-grammar account owned by `reckon/crew/metering.py:62` (`_CLAUDE_INPUT_FIELDS`) and the first-turn transcript read owned by `reckon/crew/carryover_census.py`; it extends neither, so the §3 target (~half the baseline, ~10,242 tokens) is computed by a second account that cannot be reconciled with the run-ledger figures those owners produce

response_events.reason: Valid, and recurring: the same duplicate-capability findings (token accounting re-derived beside reckon/crew/metering.py and reckon/velocity.py; the rule census spread across one-shot scripts) were raised by four design reviews since 2026-10-04 and never answered. rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the §2 classification capability is spread across seven shallow per-figure scripts rather than one module with a small interface, so the "before" count a §3 rewrite must be compared against is produced by scripts with no common entry point.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the token measure the §3 done-when is graded by re-implementts the Claude-grammar transcript account that `reckon/crew/metering.py` already owns, rather than extending it.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; the plan adds no member of any family, because the scripts it introduces live under `docs/figures/` and `docs/research/data/`, outside the `reckon/` tree `reckon/interface_counts.py` parses, and §3 removes prose rather than writing reckon code.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 and §3 add a sentence census and a per-session transcript token measure without recording any search for an existing mechanism; §3 names only `tests/test_skill_contract_parity.py`, and neither the census nor the token instrument cites an existing owner for the job it does.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3 deletes prose rather than layering over it, and the plan proposes no new wrapper around existing machinery; there is no thin layer to justify.
